evidence.claim: In 2022 Russia recorded 97% basic drinking water coverage, 89% basic sanitation coverage, 76% safely managed drinking water coverage, 61% safely managed sanitation coverage, and 0% open defecation.
evidence.title: Child-Related SDG Progress Assessment for Russian Federation
evidence.excerpt: In 2022 Russia recorded 97% basic drinking water coverage, 89% basic sanitation coverage, 76% safely managed drinking water coverage, 61% safely managed sanitation coverage, and 0% open defecation.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: UNICEF’s country dashboard publishes explicit indicator values for the target year.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Country-year welfare baseline; not uniquely attributable to Putin, but relevant to the ruler-period record.
contrary_evidence: UNICEF flags very high effort still needed to meet 2030 targets, so service coverage remains imperfect.

evidence.claim: Russia’s child-health and schooling indicators were strong by 2022: DTP3 and MCV1 were both 97%, under-five mortality was 5 per 1,000 live births, neonatal mortality was 2, skilled birth attendance was 100% in 2020, lower-secondary completion was 100% in 2020, and upper-secondary completion was 91% in 2020.
evidence.title: Child-Related SDG Progress Assessment for Russian Federation
evidence.excerpt: Russia’s child-health and schooling indicators were strong by 2022: DTP3 and MCV1 were both 97%, under-five mortality was 5 per 1,000 live births, neonatal mortality was 2, skilled birth attendance was 100% in 2020, lower-secondary completion was 100% in 2020, and upper-secondary completion was 91% in 2020.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: UNICEF’s page provides explicit values drawn from internationally comparable data series.
evidence.period_fit: Mostly 2022, with clearly labeled adjacent-year measures where shown on the page.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Baseline and outcome context; attribution to Putin is indirect and should be paired with policy evidence.
contrary_evidence: The same page marks several education and health targets as still requiring effort, so the picture is not uniformly strong.

evidence.claim: Russia reported 0% children in extreme poverty in 2022, 12% of children below the national poverty line in 2020, and 100% child coverage by social protection floors/systems in 2020.
evidence.title: Child-Related SDG Progress Assessment for Russian Federation
evidence.excerpt: Russia reported 0% children in extreme poverty in 2022, 12% of children below the national poverty line in 2020, and 100% child coverage by social protection floors/systems in 2020.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: UNICEF’s dashboard summarizes comparable child-poverty and social-protection indicators with explicit values and years.
evidence.period_fit: Mostly 2022, with adjacent-year child-poverty and social-protection indicators explicitly labeled on the page.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Baseline/outcome context; social protection coverage may reflect inherited systems as well as 2022 policy choices.
contrary_evidence: The dashboard also shows that child-poverty and social-protection data are incomplete in some adjacent dimensions, so this should not be over-read as comprehensive welfare success.

evidence.claim: The Russian Federation has universal health coverage with free care in state and municipal facilities, but quality and availability vary widely by region; prescriptions usually require patient payment except for some protected groups, and since 2019 reforms have focused on improving primary care access, especially in rural areas.
evidence.title: Russian Federation health system information
evidence.publisher: WHO European Observatory on Health Systems and Policies
evidence.excerpt: The Russian Federation has universal health coverage with free care in state and municipal facilities, but quality and availability vary widely by region; prescriptions usually require patient payment except for some protected groups, and since 2019 reforms have focused on improving primary care access, especially in rural areas.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: The Observatory is a specialist WHO-affiliated health-system reference and the claims are explicit on the page.
evidence.period_fit: System description is stable context for 2022, not a one-off event.
evidence.ruler_attribution: System-level context rather than direct ruler attribution; useful for judging what feasible improvements Putin could have delivered.
contrary_evidence: The same source says service quality and availability vary widely by region, which limits any claim of uniform access.

evidence.claim: The World Bank said Russia needed deeper human-capital gains and better public services, because life expectancy, especially for men, was low and regional and socioeconomic health differences were large; it also said social assistance should be focused more on the most vulnerable, and that pensions had a low adequacy problem.
evidence.title: Systematic Country Diagnostic for the Russian Federation: Pathways to Inclusive Growth
evidence.excerpt: The World Bank said Russia needed deeper human-capital gains and better public services, because life expectancy, especially for men, was low and regional and socioeconomic health differences were large; it also said social assistance should be focused more on the most vulnerable, and that pensions had a low adequacy problem.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: The diagnostic is a World Bank synthesis of policy-relevant evidence and states the conclusions directly.
evidence.period_fit: Pre-2022 baseline context, useful for judging 2022 ruler-period change and feasible policy space.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Context and constraint evidence, not direct proof of 2022 action.
contrary_evidence: This is a diagnostic, so it identifies problems and policy needs rather than demonstrating that Putin corrected them in 2022.

evidence.claim: The World Bank said most children, and especially poor children, could lose up to six months of learning from school disruptions, with under-represented students more likely to drop out or finish with lower qualifications and with widened inequity in learning outcomes.
evidence.title: COVID-19 (Coronavirus) Policy Response to Addressing Learning Gaps and Inequalities in Russia
evidence.excerpt: The World Bank said most children, and especially poor children, could lose up to six months of learning from school disruptions, with under-represented students more likely to drop out or finish with lower qualifications and with widened inequity in learning outcomes.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: The World Bank page is explicit about the education shock and distributional effects.
evidence.period_fit: Pandemic-era background that shaped 2022 human-development outcomes.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Contextual rather than direct 2022 Putin attribution; useful because the government’s response had to operate under these conditions.
contrary_evidence: The page notes some distance learning existed, so the loss was not total or uniform.

evidence.claim: The World Bank reported that 38% of Russian schools lacked workshops, 46% lacked scientific laboratories, and 77% lacked dedicated spaces for integrated lessons that support teamwork and skill development.
evidence.title: New Skills Development Key to Further Improving Students’ Learning Outcomes, Says World Bank Report
evidence.excerpt: The World Bank reported that 38% of Russian schools lacked workshops, 46% lacked scientific laboratories, and 77% lacked dedicated spaces for integrated lessons that support teamwork and skill development.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: The press release gives direct numeric findings from the underlying report.
evidence.period_fit: Pre-2022 system-quality context relevant to 2022 outcomes.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Context for inherited constraints; not direct evidence of 2022 Putin action.
contrary_evidence: The report also says Russian students are often strong academically, so the issue is quality and modern skills, not universal failure.

evidence.claim: Russia’s 2022 child welfare profile still showed major service needs despite strong averages, including very high effort required to hit water and sanitation targets and only partial child-poverty progress in the 2020-2022 data series.
evidence.title: Russian Federation - Demographic and socioeconomic outcome data in UNICEF country profile
evidence.excerpt: Russia’s 2022 child welfare profile still showed major service needs despite strong averages, including very high effort required to hit water and sanitation targets and only partial child-poverty progress in the 2020-2022 data series.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Same UNICEF country dashboard; this claim synthesizes the table’s explicit target-effort labels rather than drawing a new inference.
evidence.period_fit: 2022 target-year fit is explicit on the page.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Context, not direct attribution; helpful for interpreting the baseline-adjusted welfare record.
contrary_evidence: The same page marks some targets as already met, so the record is mixed rather than uniformly poor.

evidence.claim: Putin signed a decree introducing financial benefits for people who left Ukrainian territory for Russia, including monthly pension payments of 10,000 roubles for people forced to leave Ukraine, disability support, and a one-off payment for pregnant women.
evidence.title: Putin orders benefit payments for people arriving in Russia from Ukraine
evidence.excerpt: Putin signed a decree introducing financial benefits for people who left Ukrainian territory for Russia, including monthly pension payments of 10,000 roubles for people forced to leave Ukraine, disability support, and a one-off payment for pregnant women.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Reuters is reliable reporting and the page states the decree’s terms explicitly, though it is a syndicated host page.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Direct Putin action, but the policy was tied to people displaced from Ukraine rather than the general Russian population.
contrary_evidence: The same report links the benefit policy to Russia-backed territorial claims in Ukraine, so the measure may also have a strategic or political purpose.

evidence.claim: Rosstat data reported by Reuters showed real disposable incomes fell 1% in 2022, retail sales slumped 6.7%, and unemployment stayed at a record low 3.7% in December.
evidence.title: Russia's 2022 economic fall seen in lower incomes, slumping consumer demand
evidence.excerpt: Rosstat data reported by Reuters showed real disposable incomes fell 1% in 2022, retail sales slumped 6.7%, and unemployment stayed at a record low 3.7% in December.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Reuters is reliable and the article reports specific Rosstat figures on household income and demand.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Outcome context for the Putin period; not a pure policy attribution by itself.
contrary_evidence: The same article says unemployment remained very low, so the welfare picture is mixed rather than uniformly deteriorating.

evidence.claim: Russia recorded a 2022 budget deficit of 2.3% of GDP and had to draw on its rainy-day fund while diverting more funds toward security and defence.
evidence.title: Russia says budget deficit hit 2.3% of GDP in 2022
evidence.excerpt: Russia recorded a 2022 budget deficit of 2.3% of GDP and had to draw on its rainy-day fund while diverting more funds toward security and defence.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Reuters reports official fiscal data and the fiscal tradeoff is explicit on the page.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Useful for judging 2022 fiscal capacity and tradeoffs under Putin.
contrary_evidence: A deficit is not automatically mismanagement; the same report says it reflected war-related spending pressures.

evidence.claim: Putin said budget spending was up 20% on the previous year, predicted only about a 2% GDP decline, and acknowledged that economic hardships remained for many Russians.
evidence.title: Putin says Russia will post budget surplus this year, GDP to decline around 2%
evidence.excerpt: Putin said budget spending was up 20% on the previous year, predicted only about a 2% GDP decline, and acknowledged that economic hardships remained for many Russians.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Reuters-transmitted reporting on a Putin speech, with explicit numerical claims and a clear acknowledgment of hardship.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Direct Putin rhetoric and self-assessment, though it remains self-serving official speech evidence.
contrary_evidence: This is self-reporting by Putin, so it should be weighed against independent outcome evidence rather than taken at face value.

evidence.claim: The IMF said Russia’s invasion of Ukraine was part of the broader cost-of-living crisis weighing on the outlook and that fiscal policy should help alleviate cost-of-living pressures while keeping policy sufficiently tight.
evidence.title: World Economic Outlook Report 10/11/2022
evidence.excerpt: The IMF said Russia’s invasion of Ukraine was part of the broader cost-of-living crisis weighing on the outlook and that fiscal policy should help alleviate cost-of-living pressures while keeping policy sufficiently tight.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: The IMF report directly states the macro policy guidance and the role of the war in the cost-of-living crisis.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Context rather than direct Putin attribution; relevant to the shock environment he had to manage.
contrary_evidence: The IMF’s advice is generic across countries, so it does not by itself prove good or bad Russian implementation.

evidence.claim: UNDP said the ongoing pandemic had reversed human development in almost every country and that war in Ukraine and elsewhere had created more human suffering and a worldwide cost-of-living crisis.
evidence.title: Human Development Report 2021-22
evidence.excerpt: UNDP said the ongoing pandemic had reversed human development in almost every country and that war in Ukraine and elsewhere had created more human suffering and a worldwide cost-of-living crisis.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: UNDP’s report states the macro-human-development context directly and dates it clearly.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Context only, not a direct Putin-policy finding.
contrary_evidence: The report is global and not Russia-specific, so it should be used only as background, not as ruler-level proof.

evidence.claim: The World Bank’s Russia advisory platform describes its health work as expanding access to affordable health care, and its social-protection work as covering safety nets, pensions, labor programs, and delivery systems such as targeting, payments, governance, monitoring, and evaluation.
evidence.title: Reimbursable Advisory Services in Russia
evidence.excerpt: The World Bank’s Russia advisory platform describes its health work as expanding access to affordable health care, and its social-protection work as covering safety nets, pensions, labor programs, and delivery systems such as targeting, payments, governance, monitoring, and evaluation.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: The page is a World Bank description of its Russia-facing advisory portfolio, useful for policy context and implementation design.
evidence.period_fit: Still relevant to the 2022 institutional environment.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Context only; it shows what policy tools existed, not that Putin used them well.
contrary_evidence: This is an advisory-program page, so it is weaker on actual 2022 delivery outcomes than on policy capacity.

evidence.claim: Rosstat reported that in 2022 Russia recorded 1,306,162 births, 1,905,778 deaths, and a natural decrease of 599,616 people, with deaths down 22.1 percent from 2021.
evidence.title: Росстат представляет данные о естественном движении населения в декабре 2022 года
evidence.excerpt: Rosstat reported that in 2022 Russia recorded 1,306,162 births, 1,905,778 deaths, and a natural decrease of 599,616 people, with deaths down 22.1 percent from 2021.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Primary official statistics release with precise annual demographic totals.
evidence.ruler_attribution: indirect to Putin; the figures are official outcomes of the state statistical system and wartime context rather than a personal decree
contrary_evidence: The release also shows continued population decline despite the improvement versus 2021.

evidence.claim: Rosstat said 2022 poverty was 10.5 percent, or 15.3 million people, and attributed the decline to higher social payments and targeted social programs along with wage and pension growth.
evidence.title: Росстат представляет информацию о границе бедности в IV квартале 2022 года
evidence.excerpt: Rosstat said 2022 poverty was 10.5 percent, or 15.3 million people, and attributed the decline to higher social payments and targeted social programs along with wage and pension growth.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Official statistics page with specific poverty and policy-cause language, but the exact publication date was not visible in the accessible snippet.
evidence.ruler_attribution: mixed; the outcome reflects Putin-era social policy, but also inflation and broader income dynamics
contrary_evidence: The same page shows poverty remained large in absolute terms, so this is an improvement rather than a solved problem.

evidence.claim: The government indexed pensions, the subsistence minimum, and the minimum wage by 10 percent from 1 June 2022, explicitly saying the decision was taken on Putin's order.
evidence.title: Правительство проиндексировало пенсии, прожиточный минимум и минимальный размер оплаты труда на 10%
evidence.excerpt: The government indexed pensions, the subsistence minimum, and the minimum wage by 10 percent from 1 June 2022, explicitly saying the decision was taken on Putin's order.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Official government decree with a clear policy change and attribution, though the page itself timed out on direct open.
evidence.ruler_attribution: directly attributable to Putin's order and the government's implementation
contrary_evidence: This is compensatory crisis policy, not proof of a durable welfare improvement on its own.

evidence.claim: Putin instructed the government to assess families whose members lost jobs, expand access to social support for families with children, provide additional unemployment support, index pensions and benefits, raise wages and the minimum wage, and allocate extra federal funds for regional infrastructure and domestic-demand support.
evidence.title: Instructions following a meeting on socioeconomic support for regions
evidence.excerpt: Putin instructed the government to assess families whose members lost jobs, expand access to social support for families with children, provide additional unemployment support, index pensions and benefits, raise wages and the minimum wage, and allocate extra federal funds for regional infrastructure and domestic-demand support.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Official presidential instructions with specific policy tasks; the page timed out on direct open but the search snippet was detailed and attributable.
evidence.ruler_attribution: direct presidential instruction to the government and regions
contrary_evidence: The instructions show response to shock and hardship, not an unambiguous preplanned welfare expansion.

evidence.claim: The ministry said 588,000 budget-funded university places were allocated in 2022, the largest number in 10-15 years, plus 30,000 extra master's places for priority programs because of the difficult geopolitical situation.
evidence.title: Валерий Фальков: в этом году было выделено самое большое количество бюджетных мест за последние 10-15 лет
evidence.publisher: Министерство науки и высшего образования Российской Федерации
evidence.excerpt: The ministry said 588,000 budget-funded university places were allocated in 2022, the largest number in 10-15 years, plus 30,000 extra master's places for priority programs because of the difficult geopolitical situation.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Official ministry press release with a concrete allocation figure, but the page returned a 502 on direct open and is retained from the search snippet.
evidence.ruler_attribution: indirect but substantial; this reflects Putin-era education policy priorities implemented through the ministry
contrary_evidence: The release proves input and allocation, not that quality or labor-market outcomes improved equally.

evidence.claim: Putin approved instructions to assess unemployed families' financial status so social support could be provided, improve access to support for families with children whose income had fallen, add extra indexation for pensions, social benefits and wages at state and municipal organizations, raise the minimum wage and subsistence minimum, and allocate federal funds to reduce poverty and income inequality in 2022.
evidence.title: Instructions following a meeting on socioeconomic support for regions
evidence.excerpt: Putin approved instructions to assess unemployed families' financial status so social support could be provided, improve access to support for families with children whose income had fallen, add extra indexation for pensions, social benefits and wages at state and municipal organizations, raise the minimum wage and subsistence minimum, and allocate federal funds to reduce poverty and income inequality in 2022.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Direct presidential instructions published on the Kremlin site with concrete 2022 policy mandates.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Direct Putin instruction, with implementation delegated to the government and regions.
contrary_evidence: The same instructions were largely crisis-response measures under war and sanctions pressure, not evidence of preplanned prosperity building.

evidence.claim: The Russian government said that from 1 June 2022 insurance pensions for non-working pensioners, the subsistence minimum and the minimum wage would all rise by 10%, and that the decision was taken on Putin's instruction.
evidence.title: Government indexed pensions, the subsistence minimum and the minimum wage by 10%
evidence.excerpt: The Russian government said that from 1 June 2022 insurance pensions for non-working pensioners, the subsistence minimum and the minimum wage would all rise by 10%, and that the decision was taken on Putin's instruction.
evidence.source_locator: government announcement headline and decree summary
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Formal government decree summary with explicit rate change and attribution to Putin's instruction.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Direct Putin-linked policy direction, implemented through the government.
contrary_evidence: A flat indexation compensates only partly for inflation and does not by itself show lasting welfare improvement.

evidence.claim: The government said it had started paying new monthly benefits for children aged 8-17 in low-income families on Putin's instruction, with more than 2.5 million applications covering 3.5 million children and average monthly payments of 6,000 to 12,000 roubles.
evidence.title: Government meeting: new monthly benefits for children aged 8-17 from low-income families
evidence.excerpt: The government said it had started paying new monthly benefits for children aged 8-17 in low-income families on Putin's instruction, with more than 2.5 million applications covering 3.5 million children and average monthly payments of 6,000 to 12,000 roubles.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Official government announcement with concrete uptake and payment details tied to a presidential instruction.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Direct Putin instruction, operationalized through government payment systems.
contrary_evidence: The program is targeted to low-income families and does not by itself resolve broader child poverty or service-quality problems.

evidence.claim: By presidential instruction, the government said primary-school pupils receive free hot meals and that almost 59 billion roubles was spent in 2022, with nearly 188 billion roubles allocated for 2022-2024; the same package included anti-obesity measures and public posting of school meal information.
evidence.title: Government supports school meals and child-health measures
evidence.excerpt: By presidential instruction, the government said primary-school pupils receive free hot meals and that almost 59 billion roubles was spent in 2022, with nearly 188 billion roubles allocated for 2022-2024; the same package included anti-obesity measures and public posting of school meal information.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Official government announcement with spending figures and implementation details.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Indirect but substantial Putin-period policy attribution through the executive branch.
contrary_evidence: The policy is school-specific and does not by itself establish broader system quality or equity.

evidence.claim: UNICEF's Russia country page reports 100% birth registration, 91% upper-secondary completion in 2020, 100% primary and lower-secondary completion in 2020, and 93% participation in organized early learning in 2019.
evidence.title: Russian Federation (RUS) - Demographics, Health & Infant Mortality
evidence.excerpt: UNICEF's Russia country page reports 100% birth registration, 91% upper-secondary completion in 2020, 100% primary and lower-secondary completion in 2020, and 93% participation in organized early learning in 2019.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: UNICEF dashboard supplies explicit child-protection and education-completion indicators with consistent country-year definitions.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Indirect system evidence; largely inherited and institution-mediated.
contrary_evidence: Several indicators are pre-2022, so they are weaker as direct year-specific performance evidence.

evidence.claim: WHO's Russia country page reports current health expenditure at 7.39% of GDP, doctor density at 51.1 per 10,000 population, and nursing and midwifery density at 70.4 per 10,000 population in 2022.
evidence.title: Russian Federation
evidence.excerpt: WHO's Russia country page reports current health expenditure at 7.39% of GDP, doctor density at 51.1 per 10,000 population, and nursing and midwifery density at 70.4 per 10,000 population in 2022.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: WHO country profile provides direct indicator cards with explicit year and values.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Indirect, system-level evidence with long-run institutional attribution.
contrary_evidence: The page also flags worsening nurse density since 2012, so the workforce picture is mixed.
